title: Start Your Solar Business & Build Generational Wealth - Rahul Jain G2G
creator: Rahul Jain
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions (Good 2 Great by Rahul Jain collaboration video; guest Amod Anand, founder of Loom Solar)
summary: A long-form Good 2 Great business podcast with Amod Anand, founder of Loom Solar, breaking down how to start a solar business in India in 2026. Anand says there is 'no business better than solar' right now and lays out the demand backdrop: the PM Surya Ghar scheme (Rs 75,000 cr subsidy, Rs 78,000 per household, target 1 crore homes, ~50 lakh still uncovered), a 10-year addressable market of ~30 crore families, and government mandating fully domestic sourcing (90% of panels once came from China; now Indian panels are required for net metering/grid connection). He walks through four stacked business models: (1) the Loomitra referral/influencer program - zero investment, Rs 1,000-5,000 per referral depending on system size, Rs 10,000-30,000/month typical; (2) trading/dealer/distributor - GST registration, Rs 4-5 lakh starter stock or Rs 25 lakh distributor tier, 15-20% net margins in emerging belts like Bengal/Bihar/Odisha (Gujarat is saturated); (3) installation/commissioning; and (4) operations & maintenance/AMCs - a near-virgin opportunity since rooftop panels typically generate 15-20% below capacity from poor cleaning, plus solar-cleaning and smart-meter installation work (Adani and others have won smart-meter tenders). Loom Solar itself is private: ~Rs 1,000 cr annual revenue, 1+ lakh customers, 15,000+ channel partners, assembling panels (glass, solar cells, frames sourced domestically) plus inverters 3-150 kW and battery storage 5 kWh-MWh from a Faridabad base. Solar cells are now being made in India by big players - Adani, Tata - with ingots/wafers next. No explicit stock calls in this one - all mentions of listed groups (Adani, Tata) are passing industry context, and the businesses profiled are private.
